sent_prompt: /corpflow:request-plan "the test-execution gate keeps denying QA test reruns even after i've edited files in the tree. help me plan a fix before i dive in."
response:
# Plan: Fix test-execution gate falsely denying reruns after untracked-file edits

## Context
This repo already has a QA test-execution gate (`hooks/test-execution-gate.sh`, added in #303/7f10006, refined in #304/#305) that dedupes reruns by hashing `git rev-parse HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` + `git diff HEAD`. The code's own comment on `tree_fingerprint()` (line ~630) names the exact gap you're hitting:

> "Gap, deliberately accepted: content edits to a never-added untracked file move neither output. Its creation does, and `CORPFLOW_TEST_DEDUPE=off` covers the rest."

`git diff HEAD` only diffs *tracked* content, and `git status --porcelain` reports a status letter (`??`) for untracked files, not their bytes. So a new file you create, edit, then edit again — without ever `git add`ing it — hashes identically each time, and the gate reasonably (per its own logic) treats the rerun as a byte-identical retest of a already-recorded run and denies it. The bats suite (`tests/shell/hooks/test-execution-gate.bats`, D1–D11) proves the "edit re-enables" property only for *tracked* files (`src.txt`, committed in `git_ctx`); no case exercises an untracked file, confirming this was a known, accepted blind spot rather than an untested regression.

## Goal
Editing the content of any file in the tree — tracked or not yet `git add`ed — reliably re-enables a previously-denied test rerun, without reopening the perf concern ("unbounded walk") that caused untracked content to be excluded in the first place.

## Scope
**In:**
- Confirm root cause against your actual denial (reproduce: create an untracked file, get a QA rerun denied, edit that file, confirm it's still denied).
- Extend `tree_fingerprint()` in `hooks/test-execution-gate.sh` to fold untracked file *content* into the digest, not just filenames/status letters.
- Add regression bats case(s) mirroring D2/D3 but for an untracked file.
- Update/remove the now-stale "deliberately accepted" gap comment.

**Out:**
- Reworking the dedupe key scheme itself (class/invocation/run_index composition) — orthogonal, not broken.
- DV/QA authority logic — untouched.
- General performance overhaul of the hook — only the untracked-hashing cost this change introduces.

## Phases

| Phase | Scope | Why this order |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| P0 — Required | Reproduce the exact scenario first (rule out a different cause, e.g. `.gitignore`d path or stage-resolution flakiness). Extend `tree_fingerprint()` to hash untracked file contents alongside the existing tracked-diff hash, bounded (e.g. respect `.gitignore` via git's own untracked listing, cap total bytes hashed with graceful fallback rather than an unbounded walk). Add the untracked-file bats regression case. Update the stale doc comment. Run the full D1–D11 suite plus the new case. | This is a security-relevant fail-open gate — verify the real cause before editing it, then land the fix with the same test rigor the file already has. |
| P1 — Nice-to-have | Add an untracked-content smoke case to `hooks/lib/test-execution-gate-selftest.sh` (mirrors the existing tracked-file dedupe smoke case there). | Keeps the self-test's "wired end-to-end" guarantee in sync with the bats behavioral coverage. |
| P2 — v1.1 | Optional debug/verbose surfacing of dedupe-key inputs so a human can see *why* a rerun was denied without reaching for `CORPFLOW_TEST_DEDUPE=off`. | Quality-of-life; not needed to fix the bug. |

## Effort (rough)
| Size | Complexity (0–25) | Notes |
|------|-------------------|-------|
| S | ~8 | Single well-tested file, existing test scaffolding to extend by pattern; main risk is bounding the perf cost without reopening the original tradeoff, and not weakening the fail-open guarantee. |

## Risks & Dependencies
- **Perf regression**: hashing untracked content on every gate call could reintroduce the cost the original gap sidestepped (e.g. a large untracked build directory). Mitigation: bound bytes/file-count hashed, or scope to git's own (already-`.gitignore`-filtered) untracked list, and fall back safely rather than fail-closed if the cap is hit.
- **This is a security-relevant hook**: it's the fail-open backstop for QA's test-execution authority. A bug here could silently loosen or tighten the gate. Mitigation: keep the change additive to the existing digest, and gate the fix behind the full existing D1–D11 bats run before merge.
- **Root-cause mismatch**: your denial might not be this exact gap (e.g. a `.gitignore`d file, or a `state.json`/`run_index` staleness issue). Mitigation: P0 explicitly starts with reproduction before touching `tree_fingerprint()`.
- Not auth/PII/payments, so this doesn't meet this repo's `--secure` trigger by definition — but flag to the implementer that it's a security-control file, worth an extra careful review pass regardless.

## Recommended next step
`/worktask "fix test-execution gate: editing an untracked file's content should re-enable a denied QA test rerun (tree_fingerprint doesn't hash untracked content)"` — S-sized, single-file fix with an existing test pattern to extend; PL0 dynamic sizing will right-size the stage set.
